designSummary: Descriptive feasibility estimates with 95 percent confidence intervals, judged against pre-stated traffic-light progression criteria.
sampleSize: The ward admits about 309 adults in nine months; if about 80 percent are screenable before discharge and about a third screen positive (the local notes record harmful drinking in 131 of 412 admissions), about 80 patients will screen positive. An uptake of 50 percent among 80 patients is estimated with a 95 percent confidence interval of about plus or minus 11 percentage points, enough to tell a green threshold (40 percent or more) from a red one (below 25 percent). No formal power calculation applies because no comparison is made.
primaryAnalysis: Uptake proportion with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval, compared with the progression thresholds: green 40 percent or more, amber 25 to 39 percent, red below 25 percent.
secondaryAnalysis: Screening completion by detention status and length of stay; proportion receiving both sessions; mean fidelity with its interval; three-month follow-up completion (green 60 percent or more); change in session distress ratings, descriptive.
missingData: Missing screening, session or follow-up data are counted as not done for the feasibility proportions; reasons are recorded and reported.
multiplicity: No hypothesis tests; each estimate is reported with its interval against its own pre-stated threshold.
software: R for proportions and intervals; the progression thresholds are archived before recruitment.
overfittingGuards: Thresholds fixed before the first patient is screened
No subgroup comparisons beyond the two pre-stated breakdowns
Drinking outcomes at three months described only, never tested
summary: About 80 screen-positive patients give an uptake estimate within about 11 percentage points; traffic-light criteria decide progression.
